objective: Two-prefix arbitrary-repetition joint rounding: exact multiplicity caps, exact fractional resource models, constructive J-nu<=floor(a/2)+floor(b/2), and finite exact tests. The remaining nu_star-J=O(r) inequality is open; this packet closes neither admitted stronger obligation.

atomic_claims.text: Capping repeated leaves on a d-clique at f(d) preserves nu and nu_star, while preserving aggregate core-edge ownership; it need not preserve cp.
The nine-edge-type LP has value nu_star and its abstract integer resource gap is less than nine; integer realizability is not inferred.
The edge-specific joint LP has value nu_star. Its integer optimum J satisfies 0<=J-nu<=floor(a/2)+floor(b/2), by a constructive fan coloring and one discarded matching per leaf type.
The normalized two-prefix graph (r,a,b,p,q)=(6,4,6,2,1) has nu=8, nu_star=J=9 and cp=9. This defeats lossless lifting, not the global linear-gap statement.

Recorded exact computations cover all 252 positive-multiplicity parameter representations of orders four through nine, plus 166 capped-core tuples, 1100 small labeled fan-coloring inputs and twelve new mutations. The initial order-nine outer exit is unknown; two disjoint continuations complete its mathematical row coverage.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs and edge-disjoint triangle packing; clique partitions are exact edge partitions.
Core [r], prefix neighborhoods [a] and [b], independent leaf classes; missing, equal and zero-size classes handled explicitly.
Finite LP duality is a declared mathematical input; the graph-specific reductions and fan coloring are proved in the candidate.
Runtime arithmetic is fractions.Fraction under bounded processes; this is generator-side computation, not a registered verifier.
risks: The uniform bound nu_star-J<=K*r is not proved. No absolute C for the full two-level class is claimed.
The o(n^2) candidate, restricted O(n) bounds and the unrestricted ProblemContract root have different statement identities.
The continuous optimum face and all orders above nine are not computationally enumerated. Not every order-nine tuple has an independently enumerated J optimum.
